interpretation: The Palmer lag-2 performance-linked redistribution association does not independently replicate at Signy under the frozen primary comparable design.

Both mandatory sensitivities retain a positive lag-2 direction, and excluding comment-flagged nonstandard seasons yields a nominally supported coefficient, but this sensitivity cannot replace the null primary replication.
The specific lose-switch hinge is unsupported at Signy, consistent with the lack of Palmer P3 support.
The combined Palmer-Signy evidence therefore supports short-lag performance-linked redistribution as a locally plausible dynamic process, not as a demonstrated transferable Antarctic mechanism.
claim_boundary: Do not call Signy an independent replication of the Palmer lag-2 effect.
Do not promote the comment-filter sensitivity over the frozen primary analysis.
Do not claim win-stay/lose-switch in either Palmer or Signy.
Do not infer individual breeding dispersal, prospecting or cue use from colony-count data.
